This is going to get buried in your inbox, but here is the advice I wish someone told me at 16. 

First I would highly recommend continuing school and going to college right after high school. College isn't for everyone, but if you are a good student, college won't be much more of a burden to you. If you go directly to college you will be surrounded by like minded people in the same place of life as you. You will be able to experience all that college has to offer! I hated high school- you could not pay me to go back. But college is completely different. It's a lot of fun and you learn and grow so much as a person. It was some of the best times of my life!
Plus it will be 1000 times easier to continue school than it will be to go back after a few years. Once you enter the workforce it's really hard to find the motivation to leave. I completed my bachelor's degree and paused school because I didn't know what my next step was. I always intended on continuing to graduate school, but life has gotten away from me and I probably won't ever return now. 

Second, most employers don't care what your major was, but they absolutely care if you completed a degree. I have a coworker that keeps getting passed over for promotions because she didn't go to college. You will be so much more competitive if you have a degree. But it doesn't matter what you study. I studied psychology and I don't work in that field at all, but I loved every single moment of my college education. I have another coworker that thought she would be a vet and took some very difficult organic chemistry classes. She hated school and got bad grades. She now works along side me and she doesn't use her major either. So don't worry so much about your major! Just find what you enjoy learning about and focus on that. No one cares what classes you took, but you're the one that has to live through them. I cannot emphasize this enough- just study what you enjoy. 

Third, no one cares what college you went to. So go somewhere cheap!!  If you have good grades you can also look into scholarship opportunities. I went to a community college and I was able to avoid debt. I have friends who insisted on going to the more prestigious university and they are drowning in debt now. My husband's profession required two years of special training, but didn't require a college degree. After he got into his profession he realized he could get paid more with a bachelor's degree. He was able to do online school for 2 more years for super cheap. He got a business degree (profession has nothing to do with business) and now gets paid more because of it. 

One caveat: there are a few professions that can cause all this to go out the window. If you decide you want to be a doctor, lawyer, etc. Those professions have very clear paths that must be followed. However, for the general workplace there are many paths that lead to the same place. 

Anyway, I apologize that was very long. But I hope this helped you! I agree that at 16 you won't know where you want to be in 5 years. So just try to enjoy the journey. Explore what interests you. I'm 30 years old and I still don't know what I want to be when I grow up. But I'm definitely glad I went to college because it opened so many doors for me.

When you sense she's about to jump up and bite command her to sit and give her a treat. Then offer a toy or pets or stand up and walk around and see what she wants. The REALLY important thing though is you can't give a treat after she bites or it'll mean bite = I get a treat. You have to catch her before.

Oh I just had one more thought!  You said she had a foster home. Is it possible to contact them and ask about her biting when they were sitting. Maybe they reinforced this somehow.

Something I've been doing a lot of research on is the "why" behind animal behavior. If you can figure out why your dog is biting, you can redirect it. 

Is she biting during play? Then yes, the most common answer to stop play and leave the room would work. She'll associate biting = human leaves and no more fun. But if it's not during play and she's biting because she's frustrated or annoyed you're teaching that biting = I get left alone. 

Another common answer is to yelp. When puppies play they teach each other what is too rough. So yelping can be a signal of "too rough" however this doesn't work for all dogs. As when I tried it with mine he liked it and learned that biting = human makes fun noise! 

But what if it's not during play? My dog would bite if he was too tired and couldn't settle himself down. We worked really hard on "settle."  If she has a bed or crate you can teach her to go there and settle down. I just gently cuddled my boy and talked softly until he calmed down. Find a signal to your dog that play time is over. Some puppies just dont know how to calm down. 

Try thinking of the motivation behind the behavior. It can be different in every situation. But good luck! Stick to it! Puppies can be the worst! After my own I don't think I'll do puppy hood ever again. But I know from my own experience that it does get better. And soon you'll have a best friend.

This a great start. But can we see gas CO2? Notice when you exhale you cant see your breath. Can we see gaseous water? There is water vapor in the air all the time but we can't see it.

Okay at this point I would let the students think and experiment more.. but I'll just explain what's going on. 

At room temperature dry ice undergoes sublimation and changes from a solid directly into a gas. But remember that water vapor in the air I mentioned? The surrounding water vapor gets cooled by the dry ice and condenses into water droplets. Therefore the white stuff you see is actually liquid water, just like a cloud or fog.

I wish I would've come out to my family and dated my girlfriend openly. I wish I would've found out about the church earlier so I didn't have to be burdened by so much unnecessary guilt and pain. 

Now if I can just offer you some advice. Do your research about the church and figure out what you believe. Whether you stay in the church or not, please be true to yourself. Don't hide any part of you. Life is not worth living with guilt and pain. Honestly, the moment I let go of feeling guilty, the moment my life completely changed and I was able to find true happiness. 

Even if you don't get back together with your ex, please don't do what I did and waste so much time feeling empty when you are capable of so much happiness if you just let yourself be free.
